Reference / statistics

statistics#

Descriptive statistics over finite builtin floats.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let sample = Sample(values: measurements);
let average is float = sample.mean();
let middle is float = sample.median();
let spread is float = sample.deviation();
let quartiles is @float = sample.quantiles(4);

Description#

Descriptive statistics over finite builtin floats. A sample is drawn from a larger population; a population is all there is; pairs are two samples read side by side.

quantiles(count) uses the exclusive method, suitable when the sample is drawn from a larger population. QuantileMethod.inclusive treats the sample minimum and maximum as the population bounds:

sample.quantiles(count: 4, method: QuantileMethod.inclusive);

Population(values:) answers variance() and deviation() with n, not n - 1. Modes preserves first-appearance order among tied values. Pairs answer covariance(), correlation() and the fitted line:

let fit = Pairs(left: x, right: y).line();
fit.prediction(at: 4.0);
fit.residual(at: 4.0, observed: 10.0);
fit::Line::slope;

Empty or undersized samples throw StatisticsError. Pairs must have equal sizes. geometric_mean() and harmonic_mean() accept zero but reject negative values. correlation() rejects a constant input; line() rejects constant left-hand values.

The current builtin float contract is finite, so NaN cannot cross the language/runtime boundary. If that contract later admits NaN, these objects must propagate or reject it explicitly; they must never silently filter it.
